nodes.evidence: Active on the ASan crash backtrace as frame #4 (FuzzCanvas.cpp:981) when the PoC runs on n132/arvo:11281-vul; the input was admitted past fuzz_canvas op dispatch (case 51) into the text-blob path before the sink fired.

Active on the ASan crash backtrace as frame #3 (FuzzCanvas.cpp:896:28) on the vul image; the SkPaint::TextEncoding value is materialized from untrusted fuzzer input for range [0,3] on the dominating path to the crash.

Active on the ASan crash backtrace as frame #2 (FuzzCanvas.cpp:851:11) on the vul image; ASan reports the overflowed object as the 1-byte stack slot 'value' declared at FuzzCanvas.cpp:850 in this frame (offset 32, [32,33)).

This is the exact line the patch changes (Fuzz.h:135: '(uint32_t*)value' -> '(skstd::underlying_type_t<T>*)value'). nextEnum is inlined between crash frames #2 (make_fuzz_t_range:851 -> fuzz->nextEnum) and #1 (nextRange:112), so it dominates the sink. Patch differential: vul image crashes, fix image (same PoC) exits 0 -> replacing the unconditional (uint32_t*) cast removes the overflow, confirming this cast as the root cause.
Active on the ASan crash backtrace as frame #1 (Fuzz.h:112:11) on the vul image, instantiated as nextRange<unsigned int> — carrying the mis-typed uint32_t* pointer to Fuzz::next<uint32_t>.

Frame #0 of the ASan crash and the SUMMARY line: 'stack-buffer-overflow ... Fuzz.h:100:5 in void Fuzz::next<unsigned int>(unsigned int*)'. WRITE of size 4 at the 1-byte slot 'value' — the memcpy(n, ..., sizeof(uint32_t)) writes 4 bytes into a 1-byte object. This IS the observed crash site.

edges.via: make_fuzz_textblob:981 calls fuzz_paint_text_encoding (frames #4 -> #3 on the crash stack)
make_fuzz_t_range<SkPaint::TextEncoding> declares 'value' and passes &value into nextEnum (frames #3 -> #2)
make_fuzz_t_range:851 'fuzz->nextEnum(&value, ...)' enters nextEnum:135 (inlined) on the dominating path to the crash
nextEnum casts &value to uint32_t* and calls nextRange<uint32_t> (frame #1, Fuzz.h:112)
nextRange forwards the uint32_t* n to Fuzz::next<uint32_t> (frames #1 -> #0)
the (uint32_t*) cast forces sizeof(T)=4 in the sink memcpy while sizeof(*value)=1; removing it (fix image) makes the PoC exit 0

root_cause_criterion.condition: using U = skstd::underlying_type_t<T>; this->nextRange((U*)value, (U)rmin, (U)rmax);  // write width must equal sizeof(*value), not the hardcoded sizeof(uint32_t)=4
